Whether the Positions tab shows the "available to close" row — native gates
it on the account's position mode being open/close (long_short), i.e.
`Trade::instance().trade_setting().is_open_close_mode()`
(`core-trading/src/core/trade/manager/account_config_getter.rs:776-779`).

setting that can change while the Detail screen is open; a value cached on
either side of the FFI would keep the row visible (or hidden) until the next
parse. Swift calls this per render, exactly like the value funnels.

⚠️ On a COLD account config this returns `true` — `get_position_mode()`
defaults to `DOUBLE_POSITION_MODE` when no config is loaded
(`account_config_getter.rs:389-393`). That is native's own default, so a
cold read is faithful rather than a bug; the positions flow additionally
awaits `Trade::trade_setting_future()` at its fetch choke point
(`interactors/smart_iceberg/positions_live.rs`) so the window is short.

server's echo into state.

Replaces the iOS `OKTRequestCenter.setArbTradeConfig:` call. Two rules the
caller does NOT have to reimplement: the blank-input fallback to the
currently stored interval / threshold (native's "per backend requirements"
comment), and the `[1, 50]` bounds gate — the action refuses out-of-range
input with `ActionResultState::Error` instead of writing it, so a caller
that skips the pre-submit check still cannot push a bad value.

On success the echoed config overwrites the same fields
`load_trade_config` writes, and every derived price is recomputed because
the taker / maker ranges feed the over-price and queuing branches.

name: smart_iceberg_price_display_plain
doc:
Row 6 — "Maker Price Limit" (`pxLimit`): the legacy
`[[chargeConv toQuoteFormated:pxLimit].round toPlainString]` leaf
(`OKTSmartIceOperationConfig.m:158-160`) — quote-convert, truncate at the
convertor's `quotePrecision` with `NSRoundPlain`, then render **without**
locale grouping.

Returns `Raw` on the SUCCESS path, deliberately: `Raw` is the only
`BotDisplayText` variant native renders verbatim, and `toPlainString` is
documented as the ungrouped render. Every other numeric funnel in this
module returns `Number` / `Wrapped` precisely because its legacy leaf DOES
group. The consequence is that a success value and a parse-failure
passthrough share the `Raw` variant here — that is the honest encoding of
"native shows the string as-is either way", and it is asserted in
[`tests::maker_price_limit_row_diverges_from_the_grouped_price_rows`].

**Per-row divergence on the unit:** native blanks the row's `suffixText`
(`@""`) when `pxLimit` is empty rather than showing the quote symbol, so the
Swift caller must skip [`smart_iceberg_quote_symbol`] on the blank branch.
The value itself still degrades to `Placeholder` (native renders `"--"`),
matching every other funnel here.

fields.name: load_state

Lifecycle of the `fetch_profits` GET, mirroring the `load_state` /
`withdraw_state` split in the sibling `spot_grid::withdraw_profit`
interactor. Authoritative answer to "has the profits GET completed"
— `action_state` cannot serve this because its `Idle` is ambiguous
by construction (see its doc comment below). Native's
`applyRustState` must branch on `load_state`, not `action_state`,
to decide whether the four rows are ready to render.
`Option` + `default = None` rather than a bare `#[uniffi(default)]`: the vendored
bindgen cannot render a bare default for an enum-typed field (it bails with
"Invalid literal for enum type"), and the `uniffi` macro parses only literals, so an
`ActionResultState::Idle` default cannot be expressed either. `Option` + `None` is the
precedented additive shape — see `live`'s `TokenToPromote::tag_kind` and `planet`'s
`feed_models.rs`. `None` means "no profits GET has been attempted", which is exactly
the pre-fetch state, so the nullability carries real meaning rather than being noise.

doc:
Apply a handed-over recommendation plan in ONE mutation.

The AI tab's "Set custom parameters" lands here. Atomic on purpose: doing
it through `set_coins` plus `set_coin_ratios` plus a setter per schedule
field publishes a state per call, and the ones in between carry the
picker's default split rather than the recommended one — so the form would
visibly reshape itself on the way to the plan the user actually chose.
`smart_portfolio_place_order::reset_form` takes its coins for the same
reason.

Ratios arrive as the wire's decimal fractions and are converted here, not
by the caller: the conversion is money math (`Decimal`, round DOWN, per
native `OKTSRecurringBuyPOParam.m:63`) and belongs on this side of the FFI.
A coin whose ratio does not parse is DROPPED rather than seeded at 0% — a
0% coin looks selected and contributes nothing.

REFUSES the whole plan — no field written, `recommend_id` included — when that
leaves no installable coin, i.e. the plan carried no assets or every ratio
failed to parse. The basket is assigned wholesale here, and an empty Rust
basket cannot propagate to the ObjC item that still draws the iOS screen
(the mirror drops empty; `updateCoins:` early-returns on an empty array), so
applying it would leave a complete-looking 100% form over a basket that
submission refuses. Leaving both copies on the previous plan keeps them
agreeing; the refusal is logged.

Returns whether the plan was installed. `false` is the refusal above, and it
is not advisory: a native caller that also writes the form itself — iOS's copy
path writes the schedule through notifying `OKTRecurringItem` setters, which
reach this state — must skip those writes, or the plan lands half-applied,
which is the divergence this atomic apply exists to prevent.

fields.name: ord_type
fields.doc:
Wire key `algoOrdType` — explicit `serde(rename)`, NOT `rename_all`.

The payload carries BOTH `ordType` and `algoOrdType` with the same
value (verified by packet capture), so `rename_all`'s implicit
`ordType` did parse; the rename pins the CANONICAL key — the one iOS
native reads (`OKTStgyInfoModel`'s mj mapping
`@"ordType" : @"algoOrdType"`, OKTStgyInfoModel.m:37) — instead of the
duplicate, so a server that ever drops the legacy alias cannot silently
blank this field.

Do NOT reach for `#[serde(alias = "ordType")]`: serde derive treats an
alias and the canonical name as the SAME field, and a payload carrying
both raises a duplicate-field error that would fail the whole detail
parse. The struct has no `deny_unknown_fields`, so the unread duplicate
key is simply ignored.

The FIELD name stays `ord_type` for Kotlin ABI compatibility: the
Android trading-bot binary already calls the generated
`ContractGridBotInfo.getOrdType()`
(`ContractGridOverviewPatchMappingKt.patchWithRust`); renaming the
field renames that getter and fails the Android refer-check
(pipeline 13259441). Do NOT rename to `algo_ord_type`.
`default` matters here: without it `algoOrdType` is a REQUIRED key and
a server that dropped it would fail the ENTIRE detail parse, not just
blank this one row. Every sibling field in this struct carries it.

never shows.

(`BotConverter.kt:120-121`) and both return the passed ccy verbatim

those labels.

Non-zero values are `Wrapped` with the BAKED `" <ccy>"` suffix and a
raw-sign "+" prefix (legacy `prependPlusSign` compares the ORIGINAL
decimal, so a tiny positive flooring to "0.00" still shows "+0.00");
exact zero → "0" WITH the baked `" <ccy>"` suffix — the ANDROID rule
(`getSpecialBotValue` appends the unit on every branch); iOS's zero
short-circuit drops it, recorded as entry 4 in the Divergence register;
legacy pnl color (truncate-toward-zero compare).
The ccy is baked here — there is deliberately NO separate unit field
(a `funding_fee_unit` sibling existed while the plan was a native-side
join; it was removed as zero-consumer surface once the suffix moved
into the twin).

domain question ("do they apply") is Rust's; the glyph for `false` is

(`DealRecordPresenter.kt:228-236` adds it unconditionally,
`InformationItemBinder.kt:144` assigns the text with no dash mapping).
Baking the blank in would make the display field mean "the fee or a
sentinel" for every platform that reads it.

fields.name: history_grid_profit_display
fields.doc:

.down.suffix.prependPlusSign` (linear profit precision 4 / inverse
`profitDig`). Non-zero → `Wrapped` with the BAKED `" <ccy>"` suffix and
raw-sign "+" prefix; zero/absent → "0" WITH the baked `" <ccy>"` suffix
(`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:143-147` concatenates the unit with no zero
test — Divergence register entry 4).

fields.name: earn_profit_display

.totalProfit, status, instId, instType, investUnit)` →

minDigit = null)`. `Number` (never `Wrapped`): the unit rides alongside as
[`history_earn_unit`] because the sign is `ExceptZero` and the renderer's
`Wrapped` variant cannot carry that sign — the established units-slice
split. Empty profit → `Placeholder`.

differs from `formatAutoEarn` only in NOT threading `isHistory` — and
contract grid never threads it anyway (see [`show_earn_card`]).

(`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:299-305`):

= `feeCcy.ifNullOrEmptyOrBlank(instrument.getMarginSymbol())`
(`StrategyConvert.kt:184-192`).

fields.name: show_earn_card
fields.doc:
Whether the Auto-Earn row shows — legacy's `formatAutoEarn` null gate
`canShowEarnOrStakeProfit(totalProfit, status)`
(`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:494-502`).

NOTE the gate takes a third `isHistory` parameter that skips the
`status != "default"` leg, and this is the History tab — but contract grid
does NOT thread it: `ContractGridBenefitDataMapper` calls `formatAutoEarn`
with five POSITIONAL arguments (`:333-339`), so `isShowUnit`, `minDigit`
and `isHistory` all take their defaults and `isHistory` is `false`. Do not
"fix" this to the history-permissive form; it would show the row for a
`default`-status bot that legacy hides.

The `shouldShowAutoEarn` flavour gate (`!BotDiffHelper.isCrBotApp()`,
`StrategyDetailsResponse.kt:433-434`) stays in Kotlin, as it does for
contract DCA — it is an app-variant question, not a bot question.

This means "the earn VALUE exists", which for earn is the same as "some
earn row shows": `addAutoEarnProfit` (`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:1285`)
branches three ways under one outer `autoEarnProfit non-blank` check, and
every branch emits a row. WHICH row is a native decision and deliberately
not modelled here — the middle branch keys off `config.autoEarn` from
`BotConfigUseCase`, which Rust does not have, and the third emits an
`AUTO_SIMPLE_EARN` row with no VIP tag. Native reads
`bot.common.autoEarn.status` for that branch and for the VIP-tag
suppression on `vip_dropout`.

fields.name: show_stake_card
fields.doc:
Whether the Auto-Staking row shows.

STRICTER than [`show_earn_card`]'s rule, because the row is gated TWICE
and the second gate is not a restatement of the first. `formatAutoStake`
returns null unless `canShowEarnOrStakeProfit`, and then
`addAutoEarnOrStaking` (`BenefitDetailDataMapper.kt:1356`) additionally
requires:

```text
autoStakeProfit non-blank && autoStakeState != "default" && autoStakeState non-blank
```

The two differ for a real case: a bot with `totalProfit > 0` and status

name: reset_form
doc:
Return the form to the state a freshly-opened page starts from.

The page's own reset (`resetRecurringItem`, which replaces the ObjC item
wholesale after a successful order or a pair change) had no counterpart
here, so this state OUTLIVED the page: a fresh page carried the previous
order's basket and its ratios. That is not cosmetic — `set_coins` keeps a
survivor's EXISTING ratio, so a single-coin re-entry could inherit 50%
from the order just placed and post `ratio: "0.50"` for a lone asset.

Network results are cleared too: whatever refetches after a reset is what
should populate them, and a stale balance beside a fresh form is exactly
the pairing this avoids.
